title: Build a Direct-Mapped Cache
subtitle: A guided hardware lab in six checkpoints

checkpoints.title: Decode the Address
checkpoints.goal: Split an 8-bit byte address into tag, index, and byte offset fields.
checkpoints.description: Implement a purely combinational address decoder for this cache geometry. The CPU supplies an 8-bit byte address; your outputs identify the memory region, one of four cache lines, and the byte position within a 32-bit word.
requirements: Drive tag from address bits [7:4].
Drive index from address bits [3:2]; four lines require a 2-bit index.
Drive byte_offset from address bits [1:0].
Use continuous combinational assignments. No clock, state, or arithmetic is needed.
hints: Determine how many bits four cache lines require.
The bottom two bits select a byte inside a 32-bit word.
After removing offset and index bits, the remaining upper bits form the tag.

checkpoints.title: Build the Tag Array
checkpoints.goal: Store four valid bits and tags, with reset invalidating every line.
checkpoints.description: Complete the sequential write behavior of a four-entry tag array. Each line stores a 4-bit tag and a valid bit. Reads remain combinational, while reset and writes happen on the rising clock edge.
requirements: On a rising edge with reset asserted, clear all four valid bits. Clearing tags too is acceptable and keeps simulation deterministic.
Otherwise, when write_enable is asserted, update only tags[write_index] and set only valid[write_index].
When write_enable is low, preserve every tag and valid bit.
Keep read_tag and read_valid as combinational views of the entry selected by read_index.
Use nonblocking assignments written as the two characters <= for clocked state updates.
hints: There is one tag and one valid bit for each of the four indexes.
Reset should clear validity, not merely overwrite the tag value.
Use the write index to update exactly one entry and read the selected entry combinationally.

checkpoints.title: Build the Data Array
checkpoints.goal: Store one 32-bit word per cache line while preserving untouched lines.
checkpoints.description: Complete a four-entry data array that stores one 32-bit word per cache line. Its timing mirrors the tag array: synchronous reset and writes, with a combinational selected-line read.
requirements: On a rising edge with reset asserted, clear all four data entries.
Otherwise, when write_enable is asserted, write write_data only to data[write_index].
Preserve all entries when write_enable is low and preserve the three unselected entries during a write.
Drive read_data combinationally from data[read_index].
Use nonblocking assignments written as <= for all clocked data-array updates.
hints: The data array has four entries, and each entry is 32 bits wide.
A write should happen on the active clock edge; a read can expose the selected entry.
Only the selected write index should change when write_enable is asserted.

checkpoints.title: Detect Cache Hits
checkpoints.goal: Declare a hit only when the selected line is valid and its tag matches.
checkpoints.description: Implement the cache's combinational hit decision. The address decoder and tag array have already selected a candidate line; this block decides whether that line contains the requested memory region.
requirements: Assert hit only when line_valid is 1 and line_tag equals req_tag.
A matching tag in an invalid line must still produce a miss.
A valid line with a different tag must produce a miss.
Implement the result as combinational logic with no stored state.
hints: A matching tag is not enough when a line has never been filled.
The hit equation combines validity with tag equality.
Write the condition as two boolean requirements joined together.

checkpoints.title: Control Misses and Writes
checkpoints.goal: Implement the blocking cache controller and its memory handshakes.
checkpoints.description: Build a single-request blocking controller. It accepts one CPU operation, remembers that operation while memory stalls, performs the required cache-array and memory actions, emits one response, and only then accepts another CPU request.
requirements: Use an IDLE state in which cpu_req_ready is asserted. Capture cpu_req_write, cpu_req_addr, and cpu_req_wdata only when cpu_req_valid and cpu_req_ready are both 1.
For a read hit, return line_data with cpu_resp_hit asserted and do not issue a memory request.
For a read miss, issue a memory read using the saved address. Hold mem_req_valid, mem_req_addr, and mem_req_write stable until mem_req_ready is observed, then wait for mem_resp_valid.
When the read-miss response arrives, write its data into the selected data entry, write the saved tag, mark the line valid through tag_write_enable, and return that data with cpu_resp_hit deasserted.
For a write hit, update the selected cache data entry and also issue a write-through memory request. For a write miss, issue the memory write but do not update or allocate a cache line.
For every memory write, hold the saved address and write data stable until the request handshake, then wait for mem_resp_valid before completing the CPU operation.
Use a response state that asserts cpu_resp_valid for one cycle, then return to IDLE. Do not accept a second CPU request while a transaction is active.
Reset is active-high (reset=1 asserted, reset=0 released). On reset, return to IDLE and clear all saved request and response registers. Use nonblocking assignments written as <= in the clocked FSM.
hints: Separate accepting a CPU request, issuing a memory request, waiting for memory, and responding.
A valid request must remain asserted with stable fields until ready is observed.
Read misses fill the selected line; write hits update the line and still perform a memory write.

checkpoints.title: Integrate the Cache
checkpoints.goal: Connect the arrays, hit logic, controller, and memory into a working cache.
checkpoints.description: Assemble the completed blocks into simple_cache. This checkpoint is primarily about preserving interfaces and connecting each datapath and control signal to the block that produces or consumes it.
requirements: Instantiate the address decoder, tag array, data array, hit logic, and cache controller exactly once.
Use the decoded index to read the tag and data arrays, and compare the decoded request tag against the selected stored tag.
Connect the controller's tag and data write ports to the corresponding arrays.
Connect every CPU response and memory request signal to the controller without adding a second driver.
Preserve the required policies: read allocate, write through, and no write allocation on a miss.
A conflicting address with the same index but a different tag must miss and replace that line only after its read data returns.
hints: Start by matching every child port to the top-level contract before debugging behavior.
Addresses 0x00 and 0x10 share an index but have different tags, so they conflict.
A write miss goes to memory without allocating a cache line, while a read miss allocates one.
